The line $AB$ intersects the x-axis at point C, and D is a point on the line segment $OA$. If $CA\cdot AD=AB\cdot AO$, and by connecting $CD$, let the areas of $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle DOC$ be $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ respectively, then what is the value of $S_{1}-S_{2}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\because$ A(1, 6) is on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{6}{x}$,\\
$\therefore$ k=6, the analytical expression of the inverse proportion function is: $y=\frac{6}{x}$,\\
$\because$ B(3, b) is on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{6}{x}$,\\
$\therefore$ b=2, that is, B(3, 2).\\
Let the line AB be: $y=mx+n(m\ne 0)$,\\
$\therefore$
$\begin{cases}
m+n=6\\
3m+n=2
\end{cases}$, solving we get:
$\begin{cases}
m=-2\\
n=8
\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore$ the analytical expression for line AB is: $y=-2x+8$.\\
$\therefore$ For $y=-2x+8$, when $y=0$, i.e., $-2x+8=0$,\\
solving we get: $x=4$,\\
$\therefore$ C(4, 0),\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle AOC}=\frac{1}{2}OC\cdot y_{A}=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 6=12$,\\
$\because$ $CA\cdot AD=AB\cdot AO$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CA}{AB}=\frac{AO}{AD}$,\\
Furthermore, $\because$ $\angle DAB=\angle OAC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DAB\sim \triangle OAC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADB=\angle AOC$,\\
$\therefore$ $DB\parallel OC$,\\
$\therefore$ $y_{D}=y_{B}=2$,\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle DOC}=\frac{1}{2}OC\cdot y_{D}=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 2=4$,\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle ADC}={S}_{\triangle AOC}-{S}_{\triangle DOC}=12-4=8$,\\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{1}-{S}_{2}={S}_{\triangle ADC}-{S}_{\triangle DOC}=8-4=\boxed{4}$.

raw_record.original_question: As illustrated, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ (where $k>0$) passes through points $A(1,6)$ and $B(3,b)$ in the first quadrant. The line $AB$ intersects the x-axis at point $C$, and $D$ is a point on the line segment $OA$. If $CA\cdot AD=AB\cdot AO$, and after connecting $CD$, the areas of $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle DOC$ are $S_1$ and $S_2$ respectively, then what is the value of $S_1-S_2$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $A(1,6)$ is on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$, we have $k=6$, so the function is $y=\frac{6}{x}$. Since $B(3,b)$ is on the graph of $y=\frac{6}{x}$, $b=2$, so $B(3,2)$. Let the line $AB$ be $y=mx+n\,(m\ne 0)$. Then
$\begin{cases}
m+n=6\\
3m+n=2
\end{cases}$,
so
$\begin{cases}
m=-2\\
n=8
\end{cases}$.
Thus the equation of line $AB$ is $y=-2x+8$. When $y=0$, we get $-2x+8=0$, so $x=4$, hence $C(4,0)$. Therefore,
$S_{\triangle AOC}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot OC\cdot y_A=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 6=12$.
Since $CA\cdot AD=AB\cdot AO$, we have $\frac{CA}{AB}=\frac{AO}{AD}$. Also, $\angle DAB=\angle OAC$, so $\triangle DAB\sim\triangle OAC$. Hence $\angle ADB=\angle AOC$, so $DB\parallel OC$, and therefore $y_D=y_B=2$. Thus,
$S_{\triangle DOC}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot OC\cdot y_D=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 2=4$.
Then
$S_{\triangle ADC}=S_{\triangle AOC}-S_{\triangle DOC}=12-4=8$,
so
$S_1-S_2=S_{\triangle ADC}-S_{\triangle DOC}=8-4=4$.
